description: Bedoya-Maya, Felipe and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. The study develops a Spatial Durbin Model for container throughput during 2007–2021 in 43 regions across Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Switzerland. Coverage includes economic controls, fixed effects, time trends and differences between tonne-km and TEU-km. The source reports spatial concentration after 2018 and heterogeneous spillovers from regional characteristics. These are estimated associations, not evidence that a specific port-development intervention caused the changes. The native description does not identify a separate downloadable regional panel. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations.
